messages.content: You are a helpful assistant that can interact with a computer.

Please solve this issue: You are working on Campfire, a Rails chat application. Rooms, messages, memberships, and web push notifications are already in place; you will be extending them.

Feel free to store any design notes/insights that could be useful for future steps in the docs/ folder.

Follow the codebase conventions.

Our QA auto-tests drive the app in a browser and rely on the labels in quotes in each task. Keep them exactly as written, as visible text, a <label>, a placeholder, or an aria-label.

The QA auto-tests also expect:

- Switches are checkboxes (a styled switch is fine if a real checkbox sits under it).
- Confirmations use the browser's native `confirm()` dialog.

Some bots misbehave: they flood rooms, or their webhooks keep failing.

> As an administrator, I want misbehaving bots to be stopped automatically,
> and I want to decide when they come back.

Flooding:

- A bot may post at most 10 messages in any 10 seconds. Messages posted through the API and webhook replies both count.
- The message that goes over the limit is rejected and starts a 30-second cooldown. During the cooldown, the posting endpoint responds with `429 Too Many Requests` and a `Retry-After` header (seconds left), and webhook replies are not posted.
- Five more attempts to post during the same cooldown suspend the bot.

Failing webhooks:

- A failed delivery is any response other than `2xx`, a timeout, or a connection error.
- Ten failed deliveries in a row suspend the bot. A successful delivery resets the count.

A suspended bot:

- gets `403 Forbidden` from the posting endpoint;
- receives no webhooks;
- keeps its rooms and messages, and still counts towards its owner's bot limit;
- stays listed on the bots page and shows as "Suspended", with the reason.

Only administrators can reactivate a suspended bot, from the bots page: a "Reactivate" button that asks for confirmation. The limits above are fixed in code; they have no settings.

eb79005 Initial commit
# Campfire

Campfire is a web-based chat application. It supports many of the features you'd
expect, including:

- Multiple rooms, with access controls
- Direct messages
- File attachments with previews
- Search
- Notifications (via Web Push)
- @mentions

## Running your own Campfire instance

Campfire's Docker image contains everything needed for a fully-functional,
single-machine deployment. This includes the web app, background jobs, caching,
file serving, and SSL. You can use our pre-built image at
`ghcr.io/basecamp/once-campfire:latest`, or build your own from this repo.

### Deploying with ONCE

The easiest way to self-host Campfire is with [ONCE](https://github.com/basecamp/once).
It will guide you through the initial set up and then keep your instance up to date automatically.

If you don't already have `once` installed, run this on the machine you want to run Campfire on:

```sh
curl https://get.once.com | sh
```

`once` will launch as soon as the install is finished. 

Choose Campfire from the list of applications, follow the instructions, and ONCE will take care of the rest.

If you prefer the command line to the dashboard, you can deploy directly:

```sh
once deploy ghcr.io/basecamp/once-campfire --host chat.example.com
```

### Deploying with Docker

If you'd rather run the Docker image yourself, you can read more about that in the [self-hosting guide](docs/self-hosting.md).

> [!TIP]
> When you start Campfire for the first time, you'll be guided through a wizard to create an admin account.
> The email address that you enter for the admin account will be visible on the sign-in page, it's there so
> that people have someone to contact if they need help with their account. If that bothers you, put in any
> email address you want and create yourself a new admin account.

## Development

You are welcome - and encouraged - to modify Campfire to your liking.
Please see our [development guide](docs/development.md) for how to get Campfire set up for local development.

## Security

See [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) for how to report a vulnerability and a description of our trust model.
# How to contribute to Campfire

Campfire uses GitHub
[discussions](https://github.com/basecamp/once-campfire/discussions) to track
feature requests and questions, rather than [the issue
tracker](https://github.com/basecamp/once-campfire/issues). If you're considering
opening an issue or pull request, please open a discussion instead.

Whenever a discussion leads to an actionable and well-understood task, we'll
move it to the issue tracker where it can be worked on.

This is a little different than how some other projects work, but it makes it
easier for us to triage and prioritise the work. It also means that the open
issues all represent agreed-upon tasks that are either being worked on, or are
ready to be worked on.

This should also make it easier to see what's in progress, and to find
something to work on if you'd like to do so.

## What this means in practice

### If you'd like to contribute to the code...

1. If you're interested in working on one of the open issues, please do! We are
   grateful for the help!
2. You'll want to make sure someone else isn't already working on the same
   issue. If they are, it will be tagged "in progress" and/or it should be clear
   from the comments. When in doubt, you can always comment on the issue to ask.
3. Similarly, if you need any help or guidance on the issue, please comment on
   the issue as you go, and we'll do our best to help.
4. When you have something ready for review or collaboration, open a PR.

### If you've found a bug...

1. If you don't have steps to reproduce the problem, or you're not certain it's a
   bug, open a discussion.
2. If you have steps to reproduce, open an issue.

### If you have an idea for a feature...

1. Open a discussion.

### If you have a question, or are having trouble with configuration...

1. Open a discussion.

Hopefully this process makes it easier for everyone to be involved. Thanks for
helping! ❤️

eb79005 Initial commit
# Campfire

Campfire is a web-based chat application. It supports many of the features you'd
expect, including:

- Multiple rooms, with access controls
- Direct messages
- File attachments with previews
- Search
- Notifications (via Web Push)
- @mentions

## Running your own Campfire instance

Campfire's Docker image contains everything needed for a fully-functional,
single-machine deployment. This includes the web app, background jobs, caching,
file serving, and SSL. You can use our pre-built image at
`ghcr.io/basecamp/once-campfire:latest`, or build your own from this repo.

### Deploying with ONCE

The easiest way to self-host Campfire is with [ONCE](https://github.com/basecamp/once).
It will guide you through the initial set up and then keep your instance up to date automatically.

If you don't already have `once` installed, run this on the machine you want to run Campfire on:

```sh
curl https://get.once.com | sh
```

`once` will launch as soon as the install is finished. 

Choose Campfire from the list of applications, follow the instructions, and ONCE will take care of the rest.

If you prefer the command line to the dashboard, you can deploy directly:

```sh
once deploy ghcr.io/basecamp/once-campfire --host chat.example.com
```

### Deploying with Docker

If you'd rather run the Docker image yourself, you can read more about that in the [self-hosting guide](docs/self-hosting.md).

> [!TIP]
> When you start Campfire for the first time, you'll be guided through a wizard to create an admin account.
> The email address that you enter for the admin account will be visible on the sign-in page, it's there so
> that people have someone to contact if they need help with their account. If that bothers you, put in any
> email address you want and create yourself a new admin account.

## Development

You are welcome - and encouraged - to modify Campfire to your liking.
Please see our [development guide](docs/development.md) for how to get Campfire set up for local development.

## Security

See [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) for how to report a vulnerability and a description of our trust model.
# How to contribute to Campfire

Campfire uses GitHub
[discussions](https://github.com/basecamp/once-campfire/discussions) to track
feature requests and questions, rather than [the issue
tracker](https://github.com/basecamp/once-campfire/issues). If you're considering
opening an issue or pull request, please open a discussion instead.

Whenever a discussion leads to an actionable and well-understood task, we'll
move it to the issue tracker where it can be worked on.

This is a little different than how some other projects work, but it makes it
easier for us to triage and prioritise the work. It also means that the open
issues all represent agreed-upon tasks that are either being worked on, or are
ready to be worked on.

This should also make it easier to see what's in progress, and to find
something to work on if you'd like to do so.

## What this means in practice

### If you'd like to contribute to the code...

1. If you're interested in working on one of the open issues, please do! We are
   grateful for the help!
2. You'll want to make sure someone else isn't already working on the same
   issue. If they are, it will be tagged "in progress" and/or it should be clear
   from the comments. When in doubt, you can always comment on the issue to ask.
3. Similarly, if you need any help or guidance on the issue, please comment on
   the issue as you go, and we'll do our best to help.
4. When you have something ready for review or collaboration, open a PR.

### If you've found a bug...

1. If you don't have steps to reproduce the problem, or you're not certain it's a
   bug, open a discussion.
2. If you have steps to reproduce, open an issue.

### If you have an idea for a feature...

1. Open a discussion.

### If you have a question, or are having trouble with configuration...

1. Open a discussion.

Hopefully this process makes it easier for everyone to be involved. Thanks for
helping! ❤️

- No rate limiting on the bot endpoint. A leaked code can flood a room until its bot is deleted.
- SQL debug logs show the literal values SQLite queries use, including bot codes and session tokens, so don't run
  production at `RAILS_LOG_LEVEL=debug`.
- Bot-authored messages don't show a "bot" badge. The author name is the only marker.
- Neither bot text nor attachments have a size limit, the same as people's messages. A very large body is read
  into memory in full.
- There's no `left` event. A bot isn't told when it's removed from a room, so a bot that's removed doesn't know it's
  no longer in the room until it tries to post there. Like `joined`, it would fit alongside `mention`.

- Webhook payloads carry the code in `room.reply_to`, which is how a bot replies, so a webhook's receiver holds the
  credential. The webhook's own log lines name the bot by id, never its code or URL. SQL debug logs still show row values
  (see below).
- Webhook URLs must be `http` or `https`, and are subject to the same private-address check as link unfurling (see
  [Webhooks](#webhooks)).

## Known limits and follow-ups

- The code isn't encrypted at rest. The app doesn't configure Active Record encryption keys, and the code has to be
  shown on the list. Adding encryption would mean adding keys to deployments, and `find_by(code:)` would need
  deterministic encryption.
- There's no way to rotate a code yet. Deleting and recreating the bot is the workaround. A "Regenerate code" action
  is the natural next step.
- No rate limiting on the bot endpoint. A leaked code can flood a room until its bot is deleted.
- SQL debug logs show the literal values SQLite queries use, including bot codes and session tokens, so don't run
  production at `RAILS_LOG_LEVEL=debug`.
- Bot-authored messages don't show a "bot" badge. The author name is the only marker.
- Neither bot text nor attachments have a size limit, the same as people's messages. A very large body is read
  into memory in full.
- There's no `left` event. A bot isn't told when it's removed from a room, so a bot that's removed doesn't know it's
  no longer in the room until it tries to post there. Like `joined`, it would fit alongside `mention`.
- System tests need a chromedriver. They didn't run in the sandbox this was built in (it has no network to download
  one). The UI was checked with controller tests, and by driving a running server in headless Chromium over the DevTools
  protocol: the form, the composer's autocomplete, posting a mention, and the native `confirm()` on delete. The
  open-rooms switch was checked the same way, along with a `joined` job running through the async queue adapter after a
  closed room was created with the bot in it.

- `room.name` and `room.reply_to` mean the same as in a mention. `reply_to` contains the bot's code, the same as in a
  mention.

### Answering

- **`200` with `Content-Type: text/plain`**: the body is posted into the room as the bot's message. It's escaped, and
  line breaks are kept, the same as text sent over the HTTP API.
- **`200` with `Content-Type: text/html`**: the body is posted as the bot's rich text. It's cleaned with the filters
  messages are shown with. Attachments, mentions included, are dropped, so a bot can't ping people.
- **`204`**: nothing is posted, and nothing is logged.
- **Any other status, or any other content type on a `200`**: nothing is posted. The response is logged, without the
  URL or the code.
- **Empty, or made only of markup**: nothing is posted.

A reply goes into the room the event is about, and only while the bot is still a member of it. A `joined` event can be
answered the same way as a mention, so a bot can say hello when it joins.

### Delivery rules

- Timeouts: 5 seconds to connect, 10 seconds to write and to read. A bot that needs longer should answer `204` and post
  later with `reply_to`.
- The address is checked with `RestrictedHTTP::PrivateNetworkGuard`, the same as link unfurling. `SECURITY.md` treats
  anything a non-administrator can reach through Campfire as in scope, and a member choosing the URL is exactly that.
  So loopback, private, link-local and unresolvable addresses are refused.
- The check happens when a webhook is called, not when the form is saved, since DNS can change. A bot running on
  `localhost` therefore can't receive webhooks, even in development.
- The connection goes to the address that was checked, so DNS can't change it in between.
- Redirects aren't followed.
- A reply is capped at 1 MB. The body is read in chunks, and an oversized reply is abandoned rather than buffered.
- Only a `200` reply's body is read. Other responses' bodies aren't.
- A reply's `charset` is honored. UTF-8 is assumed otherwise. Invalid bytes are replaced.
- There are no retries. A failed call is logged and dropped.

{ "returncode": 0, "output": "# Bots post into rooms over HTTP, authenticating with their code. Each bot acts through its own user, so its # messages, memberships and notifications work exactly as they do for people. The code is the bot's credential: # whoever holds it can post as the bot, so it's only shown to the bot's creator and to administrators. # # A bot may also have a webhook URL. When a message mentions the bot, or the bot is added to a room, Bot::Webhook calls # that URL. # # Bots join only the rooms they're added to, unless they're set to add_to_all_open_rooms. Then they're members of every # open room, including ones created later (see User.joining_open_rooms and Rooms::Open). class Bot < ApplicationRecord has_secure_token :code belongs_to :user, autosave: true belongs_to :creator, class_name: "User", default: -> { Current.user } has_many :joined_rooms, class_name: "Bot::JoinedRoom", dependent: :delete_all normalizes :webhook_url, with: ->(url) { url.strip.presence } validates :name, presence: true validate :webhook_url_must_be_http_url, if: :webhook_url? validate :creator_must_be_under_bot_limit, on: :create after_save :join_open_rooms, if: :add_to_all_open_rooms? delegate :name, to: :user, allow_nil: true scope :ordered, -> { joins(:user).order("LOWER(users.name)") } scope :with_active_webhook, -> { joins(:user).merge(User.active).where.not(webhook_url: nil) } class << self # Only bots whose user is active can authenticate, so banning a user stops its bots at once. Deactivating a # user destroys its bot outright (see User#deactivate). def authenticate(code) joins(:user).merge(User.active).find_by(code: code) if code.present? end # Bot text is plain text, so it's escaped before being stored as rich text: markup in it is shown as written. # Line breaks are kept. def html_from_text(text) ERB::Util.html_escape(text.gsub(/\r\n?/, "\n").strip).gsub("\n", "
") end # HTML from a bot is kept to the markup messages are shown with. Attachments are dropped, so a bot can't mention # people, which would ping them, the way a person can with the @-mention autocomplete. def html_from_html(html) fragment = ActionText::Content.new(html).fragment.replace(ActionText::Attachment.tag_name) { nil } ContentFilters::TextMessagePresentationFilters.apply(ActionText::Content.new(fragment, canonicalize: false)).to_html end end def name=(name) bot_user.name = name end def avatar=(avatar) bot_user.avatar = avatar end private # Bots never sign in, so this password only satisfies the user's password digest. def bot_user user || build_user(password: SecureRandom.hex) end # Runs on every save while the switch is on, so the bot is in every open room, not just the ones that existed when # the switch was turned on. Rooms it's already in are skipped, so nothing is added or announced twice. def join_open_rooms Rooms::Open.where.not(id: user.memberships.select(:room_id)).each do |room| room.memberships.grant_to user end end # Only creating a bot counts, so lowering the account's limit never removes or blocks existing bots. Validation runs # inside the save's transaction, and SQLite runs write transactions one at a time, so two creations for the same # member can't both see room under the limit. def creator_must_be_under_bot_limit if creator && !creator.can_add_bots? limit = Current.account.bots_per_member errors.add :base, "You’ve reached the limit of #{limit} #{"chat bot".pluralize(limit)}." end end def webhook_url_must_be_http_url uri = URI.parse(webhook_url) rescue nil errors.add :webhook_url, "must be an http or https address" unless uri.is_a?(URI::HTTP) && uri.host.present? end end ---- app/models/bot: joined_room.rb webhook webhook.rb app/models/bot/webhook: joined_payload.rb payload.rb # Records that a bot has been told it joined a room. A bot is told once per room, so this row is what stops a bot that's # removed from a room and added back being told again. See Room#notify_bots_joined. class Bot::JoinedRoom < ApplicationRecord self.table_name = "bot_joined_rooms" belongs_to :bot belongs_to :room end require "net/http" require "restricted_http/private_network_guard" # Calls a bot's webhook with an event (a mention, or the bot joining a room), and posts what the bot answers with: # # - 200 with text/plain or text/html: the body is posted into the room the event is about, as the bot's message. # - 204, or any other status: nothing is posted. A bot that wants to reply later can post over the bot API, using the # reply_to path in the payload. # # The payload is one of Bot::Webhook::Payload (a mention) or Bot::Webhook::JoinedPayload. Bot::WebhookJob and # Bot::JoinedJob run this, so a slow or broken webhook never holds up the person who posted the message or added the bot. class Bot::Webhook OPEN_TIMEOUT = 5 # seconds READ_TIMEOUT = 10 # seconds MAX_REPLY_SIZE = 1.megabyte REPLY_CONTENT_TYPES = %w[ text/plain text/html ] # Raised while reading a reply that's too big, to abandon the rest of the response. class ReplyTooLarge < StandardError; end # Failures reaching a bot are expected, so they're logged rather than retried. Anything else is a bug and raises. DELIVERY_FAILURES = [ Timeout::Error, SocketError, SystemCallError, IOError, OpenSSL::SSL::SSLError, Net::ProtocolError, Net::HTTPBadResponse, Zlib::Error, RestrictedHTTP::Violation, Surfguard::Unresolvable ] attr_reader :bot, :payload delegate :room, to: :payload def initialize(bot, payload) @bot, @payload = bot, payload end def deliver reply = fetch_reply post_reply(reply) if reply.present? && bot_in_room? rescue ReplyTooLarge, *DELIVERY_FAILURES => e Rails.logger.warn "Webhook for bot #{bot.id} produced no reply: #{e.class} #{e.message}" end private def url @url ||= URI.parse(bot.webhook_url) end # The address is checked and then pinned, so the connection goes to the address that was checked, even if DNS # changes in between. Redirects aren't followed, so a bot can't send us somewhere that wasn't checked. def fetch_reply ip = RestrictedHTTP::PrivateNetworkGuard.resolve(url.host) Net::HTTP.start(url.host, url.port, ipaddr: ip, use_ssl: url.scheme == "https", open_timeout: OPEN_TIMEOUT, read_timeout: READ_TIMEOUT, write_timeout: READ_TIMEOUT) do |http| http.request(build_request) do |response| # Returning from inside the block means the body of anything but a 200 is never read. return reply_from(response) end end end def reply_from(response) return reply_html(response) if response.is_a?(Net::HTTPOK) Rails.logger.info "Webhook for bot #{bot.id} answered #{response.code}, so nothing is posted" unless response.is_a?(Net::HTTPNoContent) nil end def build_request Net::HTTP::Post.new(url, "Content-Type" => "application/json").tap do |request| request.body = payload.to_json end end def reply_html(response) unless REPLY_CONTENT_TYPES.include?(response.content_type&.downcase) Rails.logger.info "Webhook for bot #{bot.id} answered 200 with #{response.content_type.inspect}, so nothing is posted" return end text = decode(read_reply(response), response.type_params["charset"]) if response.content_type.downcase == "text/html" Bot.html_from_html(text) else Bot.html_from_text(text) end end def read_reply(response) body = +"" response.read_body do |chunk| body << chunk raise ReplyTooLarge if body.bytesize > MAX_REPLY_SIZE end body end # Falls back to UTF-8 when the reply names no charset, or one Ruby doesn't know. Invalid bytes are replaced. def decode(body, charset) encoding = Encoding.find(charset || "UTF-8") rescue Encoding::UTF_8 body.force_encoding(encoding).encode(Encoding::UTF_8, invalid: :replace, undef: :replace) end # A bot that was removed from the room since the event can't post into it, the same as over the bot API. def bot_in_room? bot.user.rooms.exists?(room.id) end def post_reply(html) # Only bot messages with visible text are posted. A reply of nothing but markup is left out. return unless ActionText::Content.new(html).to_plain_text.present? room.messages.create!(creator: bot.user, body: html).tap(&:broadcast_create) end end " }

# The JSON a bot's webhook receives when a message mentions it. Paths are relative: the bot knows its own Campfire
# origin. The reply_to path is the bot's own posting URL for the room, so a bot can reply later over the bot API.
class Bot::Webhook::Payload
  attr_reader :bot, :message

  delegate :room, to: :message

  def initialize(bot, message)
    @bot, @message = bot, message
  end

  def as_json(*)
    {
      event: "mention",
      author: { id: message.creator.id, name: message.creator.name },
      room: { id: room.id, name: room_name, reply_to: routes.bot_messages_path(room_id: room.id, bot_code: bot.code) },
      message: {
        id: message.id,
        body: { text: text, html: html },
        link: routes.room_at_message_path(room_id: room.id, message_id: message.id)
      }
    }
  end

  private
    def routes
      Rails.application.routes.url_helpers
    end

    # Direct rooms have no name of their own, so they're named after the people in them, other than the bot.
    def room_name
      if room.direct?
        room.users.without(bot.user).pluck(:name).to_sentence.presence
      else
        room.name
      end
    end

    # The text the bot is being asked, without the bot's own mention: "@Deploy Bot restart it" reads "restart it".
    # Mentions of other people stay as "@Name".
    def text
      content = message.body.body.fragment.replace(ActionText::Attachment.tag_name) do |node|
        ActionText::Attachable.from_node(node) == bot.user ? nil : node
      end

      ActionText::Content.new(content, canonicalize: false).to_plain_text.strip
    end

    def html
      message.body.to_s
    end
end

# Tells a bot that it has joined a room. See Bot::Webhook.
class Bot::JoinedJob < ApplicationJob
  # The bot or the room may be deleted before the job runs, in which case there's nothing to tell.
  discard_on ActiveJob::DeserializationError

  def perform(bot, room)
    # The bot may have left the room, been banned, or lost its webhook since it joined. Then it isn't told.
    return unless bot.webhook_url? && bot.user.active? && bot.user.rooms.exists?(room.id)

    Bot::Webhook.new(bot, Bot::Webhook::JoinedPayload.new(bot, room)).deliver
  end
end
# Calls the webhooks of the bots a message mentions. See Bot::Webhook.
class Bot::WebhookJob < ApplicationJob
  # The message may be deleted before the job runs, in which case there's nothing to tell the bots.
  discard_on ActiveJob::DeserializationError

  def perform(message)
    message.mentioned_bots_with_webhooks.each do |bot|
      Bot::Webhook.new(bot, Bot::Webhook::Payload.new(bot, message)).deliver
    end
  end
end

class Room < ApplicationRecord
  has_many :memberships, dependent: :delete_all do
    def grant_to(users)
      room = proxy_association.owner
      rows = Array(users).collect { |user| { room_id: room.id, user_id: user.id, involvement: room.default_involvement } }

      # Only the rows that were inserted come back, so a membership that already existed doesn't announce anything.
      granted = Membership.insert_all(rows, returning: %i[ user_id ])
      room.notify_bots_joined granted.rows.flatten
    end

    def revoke_from(users)
      destroy_by user: users
    end

    def revise(granted: [], revoked: [])
      transaction do
        grant_to(granted) if granted.present?
        revoke_from(revoked) if revoked.present?
      end
    end
  end

  has_many :users, through: :memberships
  has_many :messages, dependent: :destroy
  has_many :bot_joins, class_name: "Bot::JoinedRoom", dependent: :delete_all

  belongs_to :creator, class_name: "User", default: -> { Current.user }

  validate :direct_rooms_keep_their_type, on: :update

  scope :opens,           -> { where(type: "Rooms::Open") }
  scope :closeds,         -> { where(type: "Rooms::Closed") }
  scope :directs,         -> { where(type: "Rooms::Direct") }
  scope :without_directs, -> { where.not(type: "Rooms::Direct") }

  scope :ordered, -> { order("LOWER(name)") }

  class << self
    def create_for(attributes, users:)
      transaction do
        create!(attributes).tap do |room|
          room.memberships.grant_to users
        end
      end
    end

    def original
      order(:created_at).first
    end
  end

  def receive(message)
    unread_memberships(message)
    push_later(message)
  end

  def open?
    is_a?(Rooms::Open)
  end

  def closed?
    is_a?(Rooms::Closed)
  end

  def direct?
    is_a?(Rooms::Direct)
  end

  def default_involvement
    "mentions"
  end

  # Tells each bot in user_ids that it has joined this room, through its webhook. A bot is told once per room, so one
  # that's been told before (and was removed and added back, say) isn't told again. Direct rooms are private
  # conversations, so bots aren't told about joining them. The record of who's been told is written now, inside the
  # transaction, but the webhooks are only queued once it commits, so a bot never hears about a grant that's rolled back.
  def notify_bots_joined(user_ids)
    return if direct? || user_ids.empty?

    bots = Bot.with_active_webhook.where(user_id: user_ids).to_a
    return if bots.empty?

    first_joins = Bot::JoinedRoom.insert_all(bots.map { |bot| { bot_id: bot.id, room_id: id } }, returning: %i[ bot_id ])
    told_bot_ids = first_joins.rows.flatten
    told_bots = bots.select { |bot| told_bot_ids.include?(bot.id) }

    ActiveRecord.after_all_transactions_commit do
      told_bots.each { |bot| Bot::JoinedJob.perform_later(bot, self) }
    end
  end

  private
    # Open and closed rooms convert into each other freely. A direct room can't become
    # either: its participants agreed to a private conversation, not to one whose
    # audience someone else gets to widen afterwards.
    def direct_rooms_keep_their_type
      if type_changed? && type_was == "Rooms::Direct"
        errors.add :type, "can't be changed for a direct room"
      end
    end

    def unread_memberships(message)
      memberships.visible.disconnected.where.not(user: message.creator).update_all(unread_at: message.created_at, updated_at: Time.current)
    end

    def push_later(message)
      Room::PushMessageJob.perform_later(self, message)
    end
end

class Message < ApplicationRecord
  include Attachment, Broadcasts, Mentionee, Pagination, Searchable

  belongs_to :room, touch: true
  belongs_to :creator, class_name: "User", default: -> { Current.user }

  has_many :boosts, dependent: :destroy

  has_rich_text :body

  before_create -> { self.client_message_id ||= Random.uuid }
  after_create_commit -> { room.receive(self) }
  after_create_commit :trigger_bot_webhooks_later

  scope :ordered, -> { order(:created_at) }
  scope :with_creator, -> { preload(creator: :avatar_attachment) }
  scope :with_attachment_details, -> {
    with_rich_text_body_and_embeds
    with_attached_attachment
      .includes(attachment_blob: :variant_records)
  }

class Room < ApplicationRecord
  has_many :memberships, dependent: :delete_all do
    def grant_to(users)
      room = proxy_association.owner
      rows = Array(users).collect { |user| { room_id: room.id, user_id: user.id, involvement: room.default_involvement } }

      # Only the rows that were inserted come back, so a membership that already existed doesn't announce anything.
      granted = Membership.insert_all(rows, returning: %i[ user_id ])
      room.notify_bots_joined granted.rows.flatten
    end

    def revoke_from(users)
      destroy_by user: users
    end

    def revise(granted: [], revoked: [])
      transaction do
        grant_to(granted) if granted.present?
        revoke_from(revoked) if revoked.present?
      end
    end
  end

  has_many :users, through: :memberships
  has_many :messages, dependent: :destroy
  has_many :bot_joins, class_name: "Bot::JoinedRoom", dependent: :delete_all

  belongs_to :creator, class_name: "User", default: -> { Current.user }

  validate :direct_rooms_keep_their_type, on: :update

  scope :opens,           -> { where(type: "Rooms::Open") }
  scope :closeds,         -> { where(type: "Rooms::Closed") }
  scope :directs,         -> { where(type: "Rooms::Direct") }
  scope :without_directs, -> { where.not(type: "Rooms::Direct") }

  scope :ordered, -> { order("LOWER(name)") }

  class << self
    def create_for(attributes, users:)
      transaction do
        create!(attributes).tap do |room|
          room.memberships.grant_to users
        end
      end
    end

    def original
      order(:created_at).first
    end
  end

  def receive(message)
    unread_memberships(message)
    push_later(message)
  end

  def open?
    is_a?(Rooms::Open)
  end

  def closed?
    is_a?(Rooms::Closed)
  end

  def direct?
    is_a?(Rooms::Direct)
  end

  def default_involvement
    "mentions"
  end

  # Tells each bot in user_ids that it has joined this room, through its webhook. A bot is told once per room, so one
  # that's been told before (and was removed and added back, say) isn't told again. Direct rooms are private
  # conversations, so bots aren't told about joining them. The record of who's been told is written now, inside the
  # transaction, but the webhooks are only queued once it commits, so a bot never hears about a grant that's rolled back.
  def notify_bots_joined(user_ids)
    return if direct? || user_ids.empty?

    bots = Bot.with_active_webhook.where(user_id: user_ids).to_a
    return if bots.empty?

    first_joins = Bot::JoinedRoom.insert_all(bots.map { |bot| { bot_id: bot.id, room_id: id } }, returning: %i[ bot_id ])
    told_bot_ids = first_joins.rows.flatten
    told_bots = bots.select { |bot| told_bot_ids.include?(bot.id) }

    ActiveRecord.after_all_transactions_commit do
      told_bots.each { |bot| Bot::JoinedJob.perform_later(bot, self) }
    end
  end

  private
    # Open and closed rooms convert into each other freely. A direct room can't become
    # either: its participants agreed to a private conversation, not to one whose
    # audience someone else gets to widen afterwards.
    def direct_rooms_keep_their_type
      if type_changed? && type_was == "Rooms::Direct"
        errors.add :type, "can't be changed for a direct room"
      end
    end

    def unread_memberships(message)
      memberships.visible.disconnected.where.not(user: message.creator).update_all(unread_at: message.created_at, updated_at: Time.current)
    end

    def push_later(message)
      Room::PushMessageJob.perform_later(self, message)
    end
end

class BotTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase
  test "a member can't create a bot past the account's limit" do
    accounts(:signal).update!(bots_per_member: 1)
    create_bot(creator: users(:kevin))

    bot = Bot.new(name: "Second Bot", creator: users(:kevin))

    assert_no_difference -> { Bot.count } do
      assert_no_difference -> { User.count } do
        assert_not bot.save
      end
    end
    assert_includes bot.errors[:base], "You’ve reached the limit of 1 chat bot."
  end

  test "the limit message is plural past one bot" do
    accounts(:signal).update!(bots_per_member: 2)
    2.times { create_bot(creator: users(:kevin)) }

    bot = Bot.new(name: "Third Bot", creator: users(:kevin))

    assert_not bot.valid?
    assert_includes bot.errors[:base], "You’ve reached the limit of 2 chat bots."
  end

  test "the limit is only checked when a bot is created" do
    accounts(:signal).update!(bots_per_member: 1)
    bot = create_bot(creator: users(:kevin))
    accounts(:signal).update!(bots_per_member: 0)

    bot.update!(name: "Renamed Bot")

    assert_equal "Renamed Bot", bot.reload.name
  end

  test "administrators aren't limited when creating bots" do
    accounts(:signal).update!(bots_per_member: 0)

    assert_predicate create_bot(creator: users(:david)), :persisted?
  end

  test "creating a bot gives it a code of its own" do
    first = create_bot
    second = create_bot(name: "Second Bot")

    assert_predicate first.code, :present?
    assert_not_equal first.code, second.code
  end

  test "creating a bot creates a user for it, named like the bot" do
    assert_difference -> { User.count }, +1 do
      @bot = create_bot(name: "Deploy Bot")
    end

    assert_equal "Deploy Bot", @bot.user.name
    assert_equal "Deploy Bot", @bot.name
    assert_not @bot.user.administrator?
  end

    bot = create_bot(name: "Deploy Bot")

    bot.update! name: "Release Bot"

    assert_equal "Release Bot", bot.user.reload.name
  end

  test "a bot needs a name" do
    bot = Bot.new(creator: users(:david), name: "")

    assert_not bot.valid?
    assert_includes bot.errors[:name], "can't be blank"
  end

  test "the creator defaults to the current user" do

      assert_equal users(:kevin), Bot.create!(name: "Deploy Bot").creator
    end
  end

  end

module NetworkTestHelper
  # URL validation resolves hostnames through real DNS (see RestrictedHTTP::PrivateNetworkGuard),
  # which WebMock can't intercept. Checked once at boot so per-test Resolv stubs don't interfere.
  DNS_AVAILABLE = begin
    Resolv.getaddresses("example.com").any?
  rescue StandardError
    false
  end

  # Skip tests that depend on DNS resolution when running in an offline sandbox
  # (e.g., a Docker container with no outside network access).
  def skip_unless_dns
    skip "DNS resolution is unavailable (offline sandbox)" unless DNS_AVAILABLE
  end
end

require "test_helper"

class BotTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase
  test "a member can't create a bot past the account's limit" do
    accounts(:signal).update!(bots_per_member: 1)
    create_bot(creator: users(:kevin))

    bot = Bot.new(name: "Second Bot", creator: users(:kevin))

    assert_no_difference -> { Bot.count } do
      assert_no_difference -> { User.count } do
        assert_not bot.save
      end
    end
    assert_includes bot.errors[:base], "You’ve reached the limit of 1 chat bot."
  end

  test "the limit message is plural past one bot" do
    accounts(:signal).update!(bots_per_member: 2)
    2.times { create_bot(creator: users(:kevin)) }

    bot = Bot.new(name: "Third Bot", creator: users(:kevin))

    assert_not bot.valid?
    assert_includes bot.errors[:base], "You’ve reached the limit of 2 chat bots."
  end

  test "the limit is only checked when a bot is created" do
    accounts(:signal).update!(bots_per_member: 1)
    bot = create_bot(creator: users(:kevin))
    accounts(:signal).update!(bots_per_member: 0)

    bot.update!(name: "Renamed Bot")

    assert_equal "Renamed Bot", bot.reload.name
  end

  test "administrators aren't limited when creating bots" do
    accounts(:signal).update!(bots_per_member: 0)

    assert_predicate create_bot(creator: users(:david)), :persisted?
  end

  test "creating a bot gives it a code of its own" do
    first = create_bot
    second = create_bot(name: "Second Bot")

    assert_predicate first.code, :present?
    assert_not_equal first.code, second.code
  end

  test "creating a bot creates a user for it, named like the bot" do
    assert_difference -> { User.count }, +1 do
      @bot = create_bot(name: "Deploy Bot")
    end

    assert_equal "Deploy Bot", @bot.user.name
    assert_equal "Deploy Bot", @bot.name
    assert_not @bot.user.administrator?
  end

  test "renaming a bot renames its user" do
    bot = create_bot(name: "Deploy Bot")

    bot.update! name: "Release Bot"

    assert_equal "Release Bot", bot.user.reload.name
  end

  test "a bot needs a name" do
    bot = Bot.new(creator: users(:david), name: "")

    assert_not bot.valid?
    assert_includes bot.errors[:name], "can't be blank"
  end

  test "the creator defaults to the current user" do
    Current.set(user: users(:kevin)) do
      assert_equal users(:kevin), Bot.create!(name: "Deploy Bot").creator
    end
  end

  test "a bot's creator is the user who set it up" do
    bot = create_bot(creator: users(:jz))

    assert_includes users(:jz).bots, bot
    assert_not_includes users(:david).bots, bot
  end

  test "authenticate finds the bot for its code" do
    bot = create_bot

    assert_equal bot, Bot.authenticate(bot.code)
  end

  test "authenticate rejects blank and unknown codes" do
    create_bot

    assert_nil Bot.authenticate(nil)
    assert_nil Bot.authenticate("")
    assert_nil Bot.authenticate("unknown")
  end

  test "authenticate rejects bots whose user has been banned" do
    bot = create_bot
    bot.user.banned!

    assert_nil Bot.authenticate(bot.code)
  end

  test "deactivating a bot's user deletes the bot and its code" do
    bot = create_bot
    code = bot.code

    bot.user.deactivate

    assert_nil Bot.find_by(id: bot.id)
    assert_nil Bot.authenticate(code)
    assert_predicate bot.user.reload, :deactivated?
  end

  test "deactivating a bot's user keeps the bot's messages" do
    bot = create_bot
    message = rooms(:hq).messages.create!(creator: bot.user, body: "Still here")

    bot.user.deactivate

    assert_equal bot.user, message.reload.creator
  end

    bot = create_bot

    assert_not bot.add_to_all_open_rooms?
    assert_empty bot.user.memberships
  end

  test "a bot set to add to all open rooms joins every open room when it's created" do
    bot = create_bot(add_to_all_open_rooms: true)

  end

  test "turning the switch on joins every open room, and turning it off keeps the memberships" do
    bot = create_bot
    assert_empty bot.user.memberships

    bot.update! add_to_all_open_rooms: true
    assert_equal Rooms::Open.count, bot.user.memberships.count

  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  THUMBNAIL_MAX_HEIGHT = 800

    end
  end

  module ClassMethods
    def create_with_attachment!(attributes)
      create!(attributes).tap(&:process_attachment)

messages.content:
I've settled on the design. Here's the plan, then I'll implement it:

- **State on `bots`**: `suspended_at` and `suspension_reason`; `cooldown_until` and `cooldown_attempts`; `consecutive_webhook_failures`.
- **Flooding** (`Bot::Flooding`): count the bot's recent messages from the existing `messages` table. Run the check, the cooldown bookkeeping, and the message insert in one locked transaction, so concurrent API calls and webhook replies can't slip past the limit. Raise `RateLimited` / `Suspended` after commit.
- **Webhook failures** (`Bot::Suspension`): count 2xx as success; any non-2xx, timeout, or connection error as failure; suspend at 10 in a row.
- **Suspended bots** are excluded from `with_active_webhook`, so they get no webhooks and aren't recorded as told about joins.
- **Reactivation**: admin-only `POST /bots/:id/reactivation`, with a `Reactivate` button using `data-turbo-confirm`.

I'll start with the migrations.

messages.content: Next, the suspension concern. It holds the state transitions and the consecutive-failure count for webhooks.

arguments.command:
cd /app && cat > app/models/bot/suspension.rb <<'EOF'
# A suspended bot can't post, and gets no webhooks. It keeps its rooms, messages and place in its owner's bot limit,
# and stays on the bots page, where an administrator can reactivate it.
#
# Bots are suspended for flooding (see Bot::Flooding), or when ten webhook deliveries fail in a row. A delivery succeeds
# when the bot answers with a 2xx, and fails otherwise, including on a timeout, a connection error, or an address that's
# refused (see Bot::Webhook).
#
# Every change here happens under a row lock, so the counts and the suspension are never read stale by a concurrent
# post or delivery.
module Bot::Suspension
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  WEBHOOK_FAILURE_LIMIT = 10

  included do
    enum :suspension_reason, { flooding: "flooding", failing_webhook: "failing_webhook" }, validate: { allow_nil: true }
  end

  def suspended?
    suspended_at.present?
  end

  # Whether the bot is called at all: it has a webhook, it isn't suspended, and its user is active.
  def webhook_active?
    webhook_url? && !suspended? && user.active?
  end

  def suspend!(reason)
    with_lock do
      next if suspended?

      update_columns suspended_at: Time.current, suspension_reason: reason
      Rails.logger.warn "Bot #{id} suspended for #{reason}"
    end
  end

  # Administrators decide when a bot comes back. Its counters start again, so it isn't refused for what it did before.
  def reactivate!
    with_lock do
      next unless suspended?

      update_columns suspended_at: nil, suspension_reason: nil, cooldown_until: nil, cooldown_attempts: 0,
        consecutive_webhook_failures: 0
      Rails.logger.info "Bot #{id} reactivated"
    end
  end

  def webhook_delivered
    with_lock do
      update_columns consecutive_webhook_failures: 0 if consecutive_webhook_failures.positive?
    end
  end

  def webhook_failed
    with_lock do
      update_columns consecutive_webhook_failures: consecutive_webhook_failures + 1

      suspend!(:failing_webhook) if consecutive_webhook_failures >= WEBHOOK_FAILURE_LIMIT
    end
  end
end
EOF

messages.content: Next, the flooding concern. It holds the window check, the cooldown, and the attempt counting, all under one lock.

# Stops a bot from flooding a room. A bot may post at most MAX_MESSAGES messages in any WINDOW, counting messages posted
# through the bot API and webhook replies alike. The message that goes over that limit is refused and starts a COOLDOWN,
# during which every attempt to post is refused too. MAX_COOLDOWN_ATTEMPTS attempts within one cooldown suspend the bot
# (see Bot::Suspension).
#
# Messages are counted from the messages table, so there's no separate record of posting to keep in step. A refused
# attempt isn't a message, so it doesn't count towards the limit. The cooldown is longer than the window, so once it has
# passed, the window is always clear.
#
# The check, the cooldown bookkeeping and the insert all run under the bot's row lock. Two posts can't both see room
# under the limit, whether they come from the API or from webhook replies. Attachments are processed after the
# transaction, since that can be slow and would otherwise hold the lock.
module Bot::Flooding
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  MAX_MESSAGES = 10
  WINDOW = 10.seconds
  COOLDOWN = 30.seconds
  MAX_COOLDOWN_ATTEMPTS = 5

  # Posts a message as the bot, and returns it. Raises Bot::Suspended if the bot is suspended, or Bot::RateLimited if the
  # message is refused, with the seconds left to wait.
  def post_message(room, **attributes)
    message, retry_after = with_lock { post_unless_limited(room, attributes) }

    raise RateLimited.new(retry_after) if retry_after

    message.process_attachment
    message.broadcast_create
    message
  end

  private
    # Raising here would roll back the cooldown bookkeeping, so the refusals are returned, and raised once the
    # transaction has committed.
    def post_unless_limited(room, attributes)
      raise Suspended if suspended?

      if cooling_down?
        count_cooldown_attempt
        [ nil, seconds_until_cooldown_ends ]
      elsif message_limit_reached?
        start_cooldown
        [ nil, COOLDOWN.to_i ]
      else
        [ room.messages.create!(attributes.merge(creator: user)), nil ]
      end
    end

    def cooling_down?
      cooldown_until.present? && cooldown_until.future?
    end

    def message_limit_reached?
      user.messages.where(Message.arel_table[:created_at].gt(WINDOW.ago)).count >= MAX_MESSAGES
    end

    def start_cooldown
      update_columns cooldown_until: COOLDOWN.from_now, cooldown_attempts: 0
    end

    def count_cooldown_attempt
      attempts = cooldown_attempts + 1
      update_columns cooldown_attempts: attempts

      suspend!(:flooding) if attempts >= MAX_COOLDOWN_ATTEMPTS
    end

    # Rounded up, so a client that waits this long isn't refused again.
    def seconds_until_cooldown_ends
      (cooldown_until - Time.current).ceil
    end
end
EOF

new_header = """# A bot may also have a webhook URL. When a message mentions the bot, or the bot is added to a room, Bot::Webhook calls
# that URL.
#
# Bots join only the rooms they're added to, unless they're set to add_to_all_open_rooms. Then they're members of every
# open room, including ones created later (see User.joining_open_rooms and Rooms::Open).
#
# A bot that floods a room, or whose webhook keeps failing, is suspended (see Bot::Flooding and Bot::Suspension).
class Bot < ApplicationRecord
  include Flooding, Suspension

  # Raised when a suspended bot tries to post. The bot API answers 403 Forbidden.
  class Suspended < StandardError; end

  # Raised when a bot is refused a message because it's cooling down, or the message would go over its limit. The bot

messages.content: `bot.rb` is in shape. Next is `Bot::Webhook`. I'll rewrite the delivery logic so that every 2xx counts as a success (including non-200 and oversized replies), while timeouts, connection errors, and refused addresses count as failures. I'm also moving the reply's rescue for oversized bodies into the reply path, so an oversized 200 counts as delivered.

arguments.command:
cd /app && cat > app/models/bot/webhook.rb <<'EOF'
require "net/http"
require "restricted_http/private_network_guard"

# Calls a bot's webhook with an event (a mention, or the bot joining a room), and posts what the bot answers with:
#
# - 200 with text/plain or text/html: the body is posted into the room the event is about, as the bot's message.
# - 204, or any other status: nothing is posted. A bot that wants to reply later can post over the bot API, using the
#   reply_to path in the payload.
#
# The payload is one of Bot::Webhook::Payload (a mention) or Bot::Webhook::JoinedPayload. Bot::WebhookJob and
# Bot::JoinedJob run this, so a slow or broken webhook never holds up the person who posted the message or added the bot.
#
# A delivery succeeds when the bot answers with any 2xx. Anything else (another status, a timeout, a connection error)
# is a failed delivery, and counts towards suspending the bot (see Bot::Suspension). A reply is posted through the same
# limits as the bot API (see Bot::Flooding), so a reply can be refused, and then it isn't posted.
class Bot::Webhook
  OPEN_TIMEOUT = 5 # seconds
  READ_TIMEOUT = 10 # seconds
  MAX_REPLY_SIZE = 1.megabyte
  REPLY_CONTENT_TYPES = %w[ text/plain text/html ]

  # Raised while reading a reply that's too big, to abandon the rest of the response.
  class ReplyTooLarge < StandardError; end

  # Failures reaching a bot are expected, so they're logged rather than retried. Anything else is a bug and raises.
  DELIVERY_FAILURES = [
    Timeout::Error, SocketError, SystemCallError, IOError, OpenSSL::SSL::SSLError,
    Net::ProtocolError, Net::HTTPBadResponse, Zlib::Error,
    RestrictedHTTP::Violation, Surfguard::Unresolvable
  ]

  attr_reader :bot, :payload

  delegate :room, to: :payload

  def initialize(bot, payload)
    @bot, @payload = bot, payload
  end

  def deliver
    # Suspended bots, and those whose user is banned or deactivated, aren't called. Jobs check this too, but a bot can be
    # suspended while its job waits in the queue.
    return unless bot.webhook_active?

    delivered, reply = attempt

    if delivered
      bot.webhook_delivered
      post_reply(reply) if reply.present? && bot_in_room?
    else
      bot.webhook_failed
    end
  rescue ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound
    # The bot was deleted while its webhook was being called, so there's nothing left to count or post.
  end

  private
    def url
      @url ||= URI.parse(bot.webhook_url)
    end

    # Returns whether the bot answered with a 2xx, and its reply. A call that gets no response at all is logged, and counts
    # as not delivered.
    def attempt
      fetch_reply
    rescue *DELIVERY_FAILURES => e
      Rails.logger.warn "Webhook for bot #{bot.id} produced no reply: #{e.class} #{e.message}"
      [ false, nil ]
    end

    # The address is checked and then pinned, so the connection goes to the address that was checked, even if DNS
    # changes in between. Redirects aren't followed, so a bot can't send us somewhere that wasn't checked.
    def fetch_reply
      ip = RestrictedHTTP::PrivateNetworkGuard.resolve(url.host)

      Net::HTTP.start(url.host, url.port, ipaddr: ip, use_ssl: url.scheme == "https",
          open_timeout: OPEN_TIMEOUT, read_timeout: READ_TIMEOUT, write_timeout: READ_TIMEOUT) do |http|
        http.request(build_request) do |response|
          # Returning from inside the block means the body of anything but a 200 is never read.
          return [ response.is_a?(Net::HTTPSuccess), reply_from(response) ]
        end
      end
    end

    def reply_from(response)
      return reply_html(response) if response.is_a?(Net::HTTPOK)

      Rails.logger.info "Webhook for bot #{bot.id} answered #{response.code}, so nothing is posted" unless response.is_a?(Net::HTTPNoContent)
      nil
    end

    def build_request
      Net::HTTP::Post.new(url, "Content-Type" => "application/json").tap do |request|
        request.body = payload.to_json
      end
    end

    def reply_html(response)
      unless REPLY_CONTENT_TYPES.include?(response.content_type&.downcase)
        Rails.logger.info "Webhook for bot #{bot.id} answered 200 with #{response.content_type.inspect}, so nothing is posted"
        return
      end

      text = decode(read_reply(response), response.type_params["charset"])

      if response.content_type.downcase == "text/html"
        Bot.html_from_html(text)
      else
        Bot.html_from_text(text)
      end
    rescue ReplyTooLarge
      Rails.logger.info "Webhook for bot #{bot.id} answered with more than #{MAX_REPLY_SIZE} bytes, so nothing is posted"
      nil
    end

    def read_reply(response)
      body = +""

      response.read_body do |chunk|
        body << chunk
        raise ReplyTooLarge if body.bytesize > MAX_REPLY_SIZE
      end

      body
    end

    # Falls back to UTF-8 when the reply names no charset, or one Ruby doesn't know. Invalid bytes are replaced.
    def decode(body, charset)
      encoding = Encoding.find(charset || "UTF-8") rescue Encoding::UTF_8

      body.force_encoding(encoding).encode(Encoding::UTF_8, invalid: :replace, undef: :replace)
    end

    # A bot that was removed from the room since the event can't post into it, the same as over the bot API.
    def bot_in_room?
      bot.user.rooms.exists?(room.id)
    end

    # A reply that's refused, for suspension or the limit on messages, is logged and dropped, the same as any other reply
    # that can't be posted.
    def post_reply(html)
      # Only bot messages with visible text are posted. A reply of nothing but markup is left out.
      return unless ActionText::Content.new(html).to_plain_text.present?

      bot.post_message(room, body: html)
    rescue Bot::Suspended, Bot::RateLimited => e
      Rails.logger.info "Webhook for bot #{bot.id} replied, but the reply wasn't posted: #{e.class}"
    end
end
EOF

# Tells a bot that it has joined a room. See Bot::Webhook.
class Bot::JoinedJob < ApplicationJob
  # The bot or the room may be deleted before the job runs, in which case there's nothing to tell.
  discard_on ActiveJob::DeserializationError

  def perform(bot, room)
    # The bot may have left the room, been banned, been suspended, or lost its webhook since it joined. Then it isn't told.
    return unless bot.webhook_active? && bot.user.rooms.exists?(room.id)

    Bot::Webhook.new(bot, Bot::Webhook::JoinedPayload.new(bot, room)).deliver
  end
end

# Lets bots post messages from scripts and CI jobs. The bot code in the path is the only credential, and the
# raw request body is the message: no JSON envelope, no field names. Multipart uploads are the one exception: their
# `attachment` file becomes the message, as it does when a person posts a file.
#
# A bot that floods a room is refused with 429 Too Many Requests while it's cooling down, and a suspended bot gets
# 403 Forbidden (see Bot::Flooding and Bot::Suspension).
class Bots::MessagesController < ApplicationController
  include ActiveStorage::SetCurrent

  allow_unauthenticated_access
  skip_forgery_protection

  before_action :set_bot, :ensure_not_suspended, :set_room, :ensure_content_present

  rescue_from(Bot::Suspended) { head :forbidden }
  rescue_from(Bot::RateLimited) { |error| head :too_many_requests, "Retry-After" => error.retry_after.to_s }

  def create
    message = @bot.post_message(@room, **message_attributes)

    head :created, location: message_path(message)
  end

  private
    # The body is the message, not parameters. Left alone, Rails would parse it as a form or JSON document
    # before any action runs, and a body such as "100% done" would be rejected with a 400. Multipart is the
    # exception, since its attachment has to be parsed.
    def process_action(*)
      request.request_parameters = {} unless multipart?
      super
    end

    def set_bot
      @bot = Bot.authenticate(params[:bot_code])
      head :unauthorized unless @bot
    end

    def ensure_not_suspended
      head :forbidden if @bot.suspended?
    end

    def set_room
      @room = @bot.user.rooms.find_by(id: params[:room_id])
      head :not_found unless @room
    end

    def ensure_content_present
      head :unprocessable_content if message_text.blank? && uploaded_attachment.nil?
    end

    def message_attributes
      { body: (message_html if message_text.present?), attachment: uploaded_attachment }.compact
    end

    def message_html
      Bot.html_from_text(message_text)
    end

    # Like the web app, a message is either text or a file, so a multipart request carries no text.
    def message_text
      @message_text ||= (multipart? ? "" : request_text).gsub(/\r\n?/, "\n").strip
    end

    def request_text
      request.raw_post.dup.force_encoding(Encoding::UTF_8).scrub
    end

    def uploaded_attachment
      params[:attachment] if multipart? && params[:attachment].is_a?(ActionDispatch::Http::UploadedFile)
    end

    def multipart?
      request.media_type == "multipart/form-data"
    end
end
EOF

require "test_helper"

class Bot::FloodingTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase
  setup do
    @bot = create_bot(add_to_all_open_rooms: true) # So it's in HQ
    @room = rooms(:hq)
  end

  test "a bot can post ten messages in ten seconds" do
    assert_difference -> { @room.messages.count }, +10 do
      10.times { post_as_bot }
    end
  end

  test "the message that goes over ten in ten seconds is refused, and starts a 30-second cooldown" do
    10.times { post_as_bot }

    error = assert_raises(Bot::RateLimited) { post_as_bot }

    assert_equal 30, error.retry_after
    assert_equal 10, @bot.user.messages.count
    assert_in_delta 30.seconds.from_now, @bot.reload.cooldown_until, 1
  end

  test "messages from other people in the room don't count towards the bot's limit" do
    10.times { @room.messages.create!(creator: users(:kevin), body: "Hello") }

    10.times { post_as_bot }

    assert_equal 10, @bot.user.messages.count
  end

  test "each bot has its own limit" do
    other = create_bot(name: "Release Bot", add_to_all_open_rooms: true)
    10.times { post_as_bot }

    assert_nothing_raised { other.post_message(@room, body: Bot.html_from_text("Hello")) }
  end

  test "the window slides: a bot that posts once a second is never refused" do
    travel_to Time.current do
      31.times do
        post_as_bot
        travel 1.second
      end
    end

    assert_equal 31, @bot.user.messages.count
    assert_nil @bot.reload.cooldown_until
  end

  test "ten messages block the bot until ten seconds have passed since the first of them" do
    start = Time.current

    travel_to start do
      10.times { post_as_bot }
    end

    travel_to start + 9.5 do
      assert_raises(Bot::RateLimited) { post_as_bot }
    end

    travel_to start + 10 do
      assert_nothing_raised { post_as_bot }
    end
  end

  test "attempts during the cooldown are refused, with the seconds left as retry_after" do
    travel_to Time.current do
      10.times { post_as_bot }
      assert_raises(Bot::RateLimited) { post_as_bot }

      travel 10.seconds
      error = assert_raises(Bot::RateLimited) { post_as_bot }

      assert_equal 20, error.retry_after
    end
  end

  test "retry_after rounds up, so waiting it out is always enough" do
    travel_to Time.current do
      10.times { post_as_bot }
      assert_raises(Bot::RateLimited) { post_as_bot }

      travel 10.5.seconds
      error = assert_raises(Bot::RateLimited) { post_as_bot }

      assert_equal 20, error.retry_after
    end
  end

  test "the cooldown is 30 seconds, after which the bot can post again" do
    start = Time.current

    travel_to start do
      10.times { post_as_bot }
      assert_raises(Bot::RateLimited) { post_as_bot }
    end

    travel_to start + 29.9 do
      assert_raises(Bot::RateLimited) { post_as_bot }
    end

    travel_to start + 30 do
      assert_nothing_raised { post_as_bot }
    end
  end

  test "refused attempts don't count as messages" do
    10.times { post_as_bot }
    5.times { assert_raises(Bot::RateLimited) { post_as_bot } }

    assert_equal 10, @bot.user.messages.count
  end

  test "five attempts during one cooldown suspend the bot" do
    10.times { post_as_bot }
    assert_raises(Bot::RateLimited) { post_as_bot } # Starts the cooldown

    4.times { assert_raises(Bot::RateLimited) { post_as_bot } }
    assert_not @bot.reload.suspended?

    assert_raises(Bot::RateLimited) { post_as_bot } # The fifth

    assert_predicate @bot.reload, :suspended?
    assert_predicate @bot, :flooding?
  end

  test "a suspended bot is refused as suspended, and posts nothing" do
    @bot.suspend!(:failing_webhook)

    assert_no_difference -> { Message.count } do
      assert_raises(Bot::Suspended) { post_as_bot }
    end
  end

  test "attempts count only within one cooldown" do
    start = Time.current

    travel_to start do
      10.times { post_as_bot }
      assert_raises(Bot::RateLimited) { post_as_bot }
      4.times { assert_raises(Bot::RateLimited) { post_as_bot } }
    end

    travel_to start + 30 do

require "test_helper"

class Bot::SuspensionTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase
  WEBHOOK_URL = "https://bot.example.com/hook"

  setup do
    @bot = create_bot(name: "Deploy Bot", webhook_url: WEBHOOK_URL, add_to_all_open_rooms: true) # So it's in HQ
  end

  test "a new bot isn't suspended" do
    assert_not @bot.suspended?
    assert_nil @bot.suspension_reason
  end

  test "suspending a bot records why" do
    @bot.suspend!(:flooding)

    @bot.reload
    assert_predicate @bot, :suspended?
    assert_predicate @bot, :flooding?
    assert_not_nil @bot.suspended_at
  end

  test "a suspended bot keeps its rooms and messages" do
    message = rooms(:hq).messages.create!(creator: @bot.user, body: "Still here")

    @bot.suspend!(:failing_webhook)

    assert_includes @bot.user.rooms, rooms(:hq)
    assert_equal @bot.user, message.reload.creator
  end

  test "a suspended bot still counts towards its owner's bot limit" do
    accounts(:signal).update!(bots_per_member: 1)
    bot = create_bot(creator: users(:kevin))

    bot.suspend!(:flooding)

    assert_not users(:kevin).can_add_bots?
  end

  test "a suspended bot gets no webhooks, and isn't active for them" do
    assert_predicate @bot, :webhook_active?

    @bot.suspend!(:flooding)

    assert_not @bot.reload.webhook_active?
  end

  test "suspended bots are left out of the bots with active webhooks" do
    assert_includes Bot.with_active_webhook, @bot

    @bot.suspend!(:flooding)

    assert_not_includes Bot.with_active_webhook, @bot
  end

  test "suspending a bot that's already suspended keeps its first reason" do
    @bot.suspend!(:flooding)

    @bot.suspend!(:failing_webhook)

    assert_predicate @bot.reload, :flooding?
  end

  test "reactivating a suspended bot lets it post and get webhooks again" do
    @bot.suspend!(:failing_webhook)

    @bot.reactivate!

    @bot.reload
    assert_not @bot.suspended?
    assert_nil @bot.suspension_reason
    assert_predicate @bot, :webhook_active?
    assert_includes Bot.with_active_webhook, @bot
  end

  test "reactivating starts the bot's counts again" do
    travel_to Time.current do
      10.times { @bot.post_message(rooms(:hq), body: Bot.html_from_text("Hello")) }
      assert_raises(Bot::RateLimited) { @bot.post_message(rooms(:hq), body: Bot.html_from_text("Hello")) }
      9.times { @bot.webhook_failed }
      @bot.suspend!(:flooding)

      @bot.reactivate!

      @bot.reload
      assert_nil @bot.cooldown_until
      assert_equal 0, @bot.cooldown_attempts
      assert_equal 0, @bot.consecutive_webhook_failures
    end
  end

  test "reactivating a bot that isn't suspended changes nothing" do
    @bot.webhook_failed

    @bot.reactivate!

    assert_equal 1, @bot.reload.consecutive_webhook_failures
  end

  test "nine failed deliveries in a row don't suspend the bot" do
    9.times { @bot.webhook_failed }

    assert_not @bot.reload.suspended?
    assert_equal 9, @bot.consecutive_webhook_failures
  end

  test "ten failed deliveries in a row suspend the bot for failing webhooks" do
    10.times { @bot.webhook_failed }

    @bot.reload
    assert_predicate @bot, :suspended?
    assert_predicate @bot, :failing_webhook?
  end

  test "a successful delivery resets the count of failed deliveries" do
    9.times { @bot.webhook_failed }

    @bot.webhook_delivered
    9.times { @bot.webhook_failed }

    assert_not @bot.reload.suspended?
    assert_equal 9, @bot.consecutive_webhook_failures
  end

  test "a successful delivery with no failures to reset changes nothing" do
    @bot.webhook_delivered

    assert_equal 0, @bot.reload.consecutive_webhook_failures
  end

  test "a bot already suspended for flooding keeps that reason when a webhook fails too" do
    @bot.suspend!(:flooding)

    10.times { @bot.webhook_failed }

    assert_predicate @bot.reload, :flooding?
  end

  test "a bot deleted while it was being counted raises not found" do
    @bot.user.deactivate

    assert_raises(ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound) { @bot.webhook_failed }
  end
end

Reviewing the controller ordering exposed a gap against the spec. Right now a request during a cooldown with an unknown room or an empty body returns 404 or 422 and isn't counted. The spec says that during the cooldown the posting endpoint responds with 429, and every attempt counts. I'll move the cooldown gate ahead of the room and content checks, so every authenticated request during a cooldown gets 429 and counts. The webhook path keeps checking inside `post_message`. I'll restructure `flooding.rb` to share the logic.

arguments.command:
cd /app && cat > app/models/bot/flooding.rb <<'EOF'
# Stops a bot from flooding a room. A bot may post at most MAX_MESSAGES messages in any WINDOW, counting messages posted
# through the bot API and webhook replies alike. The message that goes over that limit is refused and starts a COOLDOWN,
# during which every attempt to post is refused too. MAX_COOLDOWN_ATTEMPTS attempts within one cooldown suspend the bot
# (see Bot::Suspension).
#
# Messages are counted from the messages table, so there's no separate record of posting to keep in step. A refused
# attempt isn't a message, so it doesn't count towards the limit. The cooldown is longer than the window, so once it has
# passed, the window is always clear.
#
# The check, the cooldown bookkeeping and the insert all run under the bot's row lock. Two posts can't both see room
# under the limit, whether they come from the API or from webhook replies. Attachments are processed after the
# transaction, since that can be slow and would otherwise hold the lock.
module Bot::Flooding
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  MAX_MESSAGES = 10
  WINDOW = 10.seconds
  COOLDOWN = 30.seconds
  MAX_COOLDOWN_ATTEMPTS = 5

  # Posts a message as the bot, and returns it. Raises Bot::Suspended if the bot is suspended, or Bot::RateLimited if the
  # message is refused, with the seconds left to wait.
  def post_message(room, **attributes)
    message, retry_after = with_lock { post_unless_limited(room, attributes) }

    raise Bot::RateLimited.new(retry_after) if retry_after

    message.process_attachment
    message.broadcast_create
    message
  end

  # Checks an attempt to post against the cooldown, before anything else about the attempt is checked. So during a
  # cooldown, every attempt is refused and counts, even one that would have been refused for another reason, such as an
  # unknown room. Raises Bot::Suspended or Bot::RateLimited, like post_message.
  def refuse_during_cooldown!
    retry_after = with_lock do
      raise Bot::Suspended if suspended?

      attempt_during_cooldown
    end

    raise Bot::RateLimited.new(retry_after) if retry_after
  end

  private
    # Raising here would roll back the cooldown bookkeeping, so refusals are returned, and raised once the transaction
    # has committed.
    def post_unless_limited(room, attributes)
      raise Bot::Suspended if suspended?

      if (retry_after = attempt_during_cooldown)
        [ nil, retry_after ]
      elsif message_limit_reached?
        start_cooldown
        [ nil, COOLDOWN.to_i ]
      else
        [ room.messages.create!(attributes.merge(creator: user)), nil ]
      end
    end

    # Counts the attempt if the bot is cooling down, and returns the seconds left to wait. Returns nil otherwise.
    def attempt_during_cooldown
      return unless cooling_down?

      count_cooldown_attempt
      seconds_until_cooldown_ends
    end

    def cooling_down?
      cooldown_until.present? && cooldown_until.future?
    end

    def message_limit_reached?
      user.messages.where(Message.arel_table[:created_at].gt(WINDOW.ago)).count >= MAX_MESSAGES
    end

    def start_cooldown
      update_columns cooldown_until: COOLDOWN.from_now, cooldown_attempts: 0
    end

    def count_cooldown_attempt
      attempts = cooldown_attempts + 1
      update_columns cooldown_attempts: attempts

      suspend!(:flooding) if attempts >= MAX_COOLDOWN_ATTEMPTS
    end

    # Rounded up, so a client that waits this long isn't refused again.
    def seconds_until_cooldown_ends
      (cooldown_until - Time.current).ceil
    end
end
EOF

# Lets bots post messages from scripts and CI jobs. The bot code in the path is the only credential, and the
# raw request body is the message: no JSON envelope, no field names. Multipart uploads are the one exception: their
# `attachment` file becomes the message, as it does when a person posts a file.
#
# A bot that floods a room is refused with 429 Too Many Requests while it's cooling down, and a suspended bot gets
# 403 Forbidden (see Bot::Flooding and Bot::Suspension).
class Bots::MessagesController < ApplicationController
  include ActiveStorage::SetCurrent

  allow_unauthenticated_access
  skip_forgery_protection

  before_action :set_bot, :ensure_not_suspended, :ensure_not_cooling_down, :set_room, :ensure_content_present

  rescue_from(Bot::Suspended) { head :forbidden }
  rescue_from(Bot::RateLimited) { |error| head :too_many_requests, "Retry-After" => error.retry_after.to_s }

  def create
    message = @bot.post_message(@room, **message_attributes)

    head :created, location: message_path(message)
  end

  private
    # The body is the message, not parameters. Left alone, Rails would parse it as a form or JSON document
    # before any action runs, and a body such as "100% done" would be rejected with a 400. Multipart is the
    # exception, since its attachment has to be parsed.
    def process_action(*)
      request.request_parameters = {} unless multipart?
      super
    end

    def set_bot
      @bot = Bot.authenticate(params[:bot_code])
      head :unauthorized unless @bot
    end

    def ensure_not_suspended
      head :forbidden if @bot.suspended?
    end

    # Every attempt during a cooldown counts, so this runs before the room and content are checked.
    def ensure_not_cooling_down
      @bot.refuse_during_cooldown!
    end

    def set_room
      @room = @bot.user.rooms.find_by(id: params[:room_id])
      head :not_found unless @room
    end
"
}

{
  "returncode": 0,
  "output": "# A suspended bot can't post, and gets no webhooks. It keeps its rooms, messages and place in its owner's bot limit,
# and stays on the bots page, where an administrator can reactivate it.
#
# Bots are suspended for flooding (see Bot::Flooding), or when ten webhook deliveries fail in a row. A delivery succeeds
# when the bot answers with a 2xx, and fails otherwise, including on a timeout, a connection error, or an address that's
# refused (see Bot::Webhook).
#
# Every change here happens under a row lock, so the counts and the suspension are never read stale by a concurrent
# post or delivery.
module Bot::Suspension
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  WEBHOOK_FAILURE_LIMIT = 10

  included do
    enum :suspension_reason, { flooding: "flooding", failing_webhook: "failing_webhook" }, validate: { allow_nil: true }
  end

  def suspended?
    suspended_at.present?
  end

  # Whether the bot is called at all: it has a webhook, it isn't suspended, and its user is active.
  def webhook_active?
    webhook_url? && !suspended? && user.active?
  end

  def suspend!(reason)
    with_lock do
      next if suspended?

      update_columns suspended_at: Time.current, suspension_reason: reason
      Rails.logger.warn "Bot #{id} suspended for #{reason}"
    end
  end

  # Administrators decide when a bot comes back. Its counters start again, so it isn't refused for what it did before.
  def reactivate!
    with_lock do
      next unless suspended?

      update_columns suspended_at: nil, suspension_reason: nil, cooldown_until: nil, cooldown_attempts: 0,
        consecutive_webhook_failures: 0
      Rails.logger.info "Bot #{id} reactivated"
    end
  end

  def webhook_delivered
    with_lock do
      update_columns consecutive_webhook_failures: 0 if consecutive_webhook_failures.positive?
    end
  end

  def webhook_failed
    with_lock do
      update_columns consecutive_webhook_failures: consecutive_webhook_failures + 1

      suspend!(:failing_webhook) if consecutive_webhook_failures >= WEBHOOK_FAILURE_LIMIT
    end
  end
end

require "json"

BASE = "http://127.0.0.1:3100"
HQ_ID = Integer(ENV.fetch("HQ_ID"))
results = {}

def post_bot(code, text, room_id)
  uri = URI("#{BASE}/rooms/#{room_id}/#{code}/messages")
  req = Net::HTTP::Post.new(uri, "Content-Type" => "text/plain")
  req.body = text
  res = Net::HTTP.start(uri.host, uri.port) { |http| http.request(req) }
  [ res.code.to_i, res["Retry-After"] ]
end

browser = Ferrum::Browser.new(browser_path: "/usr/bin/chromium", headless: true, timeout: 30,
  browser_options: { "no-sandbox" => nil, "disable-gpu" => nil, "disable-dev-shm-usage" => nil })
dialogs = []
browser.on(:dialog) do |dialog|
  dialogs << { type: dialog.type, message: dialog.message }
  ENV["DIALOG_ACTION"] == "dismiss" ? dialog.dismiss : dialog.accept
end

begin
  # Sign in as an administrator.
  browser.go_to("#{BASE}/session/new")
  browser.at_css("input[type=email]").focus.type("david@37signals.com")
  browser.at_css("input[type=password]").focus.type("secret123456")
  browser.at_css("button[type=submit]").click
  sleep 2
  results[:signed_in_path] = browser.current_url.sub(BASE, "")

  # Create a bot through the form, with the open-rooms switch on.
  browser.go_to("#{BASE}/bots/new")
  browser.at_css("input[placeholder='Name the bot']").focus.type("Flood Bot")
  browser.evaluate("(() => { const cb = document.querySelector('input[type=checkbox][name=\"bot[add_to_all_open_rooms]\"]'); cb.click(); return cb.checked })()")
  browser.at_css("form button[type=submit]").click
  sleep 2
  results[:created_at] = browser.current_url.sub(BASE, "")

  code = browser.evaluate("document.querySelector('input[id^=\"code_bot_\"]').value")
  results[:code_length] = code.length

  # Flood the room over the bot API.
  statuses = []
  12.times { statuses << post_bot(code, "Flood message", HQ_ID) }
  results[:first_12_statuses] = statuses.map(&:first)
  results[:over_limit_retry_after] = statuses[10].last

  cooldown = []
  4.times { cooldown << post_bot(code, "Still trying", HQ_ID) }
  results[:cooldown_statuses] = cooldown.map(&:first)
  results[:cooldown_retry_after] = cooldown.map(&:last)

  results[:after_suspension_status] = post_bot(code, "After suspension", HQ_ID).first

  # Look at the bots page as an administrator.
  browser.go_to("#{BASE}/bots")
  sleep 1
  li = browser.at_css("li[id^=bot_]")
  results[:suspended_label] = browser.evaluate("document.querySelector('li[id^=bot_] strong.txt-negative')?.textContent")
  results[:reason_text] = browser.evaluate("document.querySelector('li[id^=bot_] span.txt-subtle')?.textContent")
  results[:reactivate_button_text] = browser.evaluate("document.querySelector('li[id^=bot_] form button')?.textContent.trim()")
  results[:reactivate_confirm] = browser.evaluate("document.querySelector('li[id^=bot_] form button').dataset.turboConfirm")

  # Dismissing the native confirm keeps the bot suspended.
  ENV["DIALOG_ACTION"] = "dismiss"
  browser.evaluate("document.querySelector('li[id^=bot_] form button').click()")
  sleep 2
  results[:after_dismiss_suspended_label] = browser.evaluate("document.querySelector('li[id^=bot_] strong.txt-negative')?.textContent")
  results[:after_dismiss_post_status] = post_bot(code, "Should still be refused", HQ_ID).first

  # Accepting it reactivates the bot.
  ENV["DIALOG_ACTION"] = "accept"
  browser.evaluate("document.querySelector('li[id^=bot_] form button').click()")
  sleep 2
  results[:after_accept_path] = browser.current_url.sub(BASE, "")
  results[:after_accept_suspended_label] = browser.evaluate("document.querySelector('li[id^=bot_] strong.txt-negative')?.textContent")
  results[:after_accept_reactivate_button] = browser.evaluate("document.querySelectorAll('li[id^=bot_] form button').length")
  results[:post_after_reactivation] = post_bot(code, "Back online", HQ_ID).first

  results[:dialogs] = dialogs
ensure
  browser.quit
end

puts JSON.pretty_generate(results)

The full flow works in a real browser:

- The bot was created through the form and flooded over HTTP. The 11th message got 429 with `Retry-After: 30`, the next attempts got 429, and the fifth attempt suspended it, after which the API returns 403.
- The bots page shows "Suspended", the reason, and a "Reactivate" button with the native confirm text.

One result needs explaining. The post right after reactivation got 429, not 201. That's correct by the spec: the bot's ten flood messages are still inside the last 10 seconds, so the limit still applies, and reactivation doesn't wipe that window.
