{
  "returncode": 0,
  "output": "## Model

- `Bot` (`bots` table) holds the bot's **code**, the credential that authenticates its requests, and its
  **creator** (the person who set it up).
- Each bot has its own `User` (`bots.user_id`, one-to-one). That user carries the bot's name and avatar and is what
  messages, memberships and notifications point at. So a bot is an ordinary member as far as the rest of the app is
  concerned: it's named and avatared like anyone, shows as the author of its messages, joins open rooms only when it's
....
## Web UI

- `/account/edit` has a bot icon link ("Set up chat bots") for every member, not only administrators.
- `/bots` lists the bots (no pagination). Each item shows the name, the creator (for administrators), an edit link
  ("Edit <name>"), and a read-only "Bot code" field with a copy button. The page is marked `turbo-cache-control: no-cache`
  so Turbo doesn't keep codes in its page cache.
- `/bots/new` and `/bots/:id/edit` share one form: avatar (optional), name ("Name the bot", required), webhook URL
  (optional, "Webhook URL", see [Webhooks](#webhooks)), the "Add to all open rooms" switch (off by default, see
  [Open rooms](#open-rooms)), "Save changes".
  The edit page adds "Delete this chat bot", which asks for confirmation with Turbo's `data-turbo-confirm`
  (the native `confirm()`).
- Forms that fail validation re-render with status 422.
- An empty file field doesn't clear the current avatar. The controller drops blank `avatar` params.

....
## HTTP API

```
curl -d "Deploy of v1.2.3 finished ✅" \
  https://chat.example.com/rooms/<room-id>/<bot-code>/messages
```

Route: `POST /rooms/:room_id/:bot_code/messages` (`bot_messages_path`), handled by `Bots::MessagesController`.

| Situation                                                     | Status                       |
|---------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------|
| Message created                                               | `201 Created`, `Location: /messages/:id` |
| Unknown, deleted or banned bot code                           | `401 Unauthorized`           |
| Room doesn't exist, or the bot isn't a member of it           | `404 Not Found`              |
| Empty or whitespace-only body and no attachment               | `422 Unprocessable Content`  |

Checks run in that order, so an unknown code gets 401 whatever the room is. A response never includes the code.

Request bodies:

....
### When it's called

- A message mentions the bot. The @-mention autocomplete inserts the mention, and that's what triggers the webhook.
- The bot is active, has a webhook, and is a member of the room the message was posted to. A bot that has left the room
  isn't called.
- Messages written by bots never call webhooks. A bot's reply can mention another bot, and that would set off a loop.
- A message that mentions a bot twice calls it once.
- Only new messages call webhooks. Editing a message to add a mention doesn't, the same as push notifications.
- Calls run in `Bot::WebhookJob`, after the message is saved, so the person posting never waits for them. A message
  deleted before its job runs is dropped.
- The bot is added to a room, by the open-rooms switch or by a person. Its webhook is called with a `joined` event, once
  per room (see [Open rooms](#open-rooms)). Direct rooms never produce one. The bot must still be an active member of the
...
### Answering

- **`200` with `Content-Type: text/plain`**: the body is posted into the room as the bot's message. It's escaped, and
  line breaks are kept, the same as text sent over the HTTP API.
- **`200` with `Content-Type: text/html`**: the body is posted as the bot's rich text. It's cleaned with the filters
  messages are shown with. Attachments, mentions included, are dropped, so a bot can't ping people.
- **`204`**: nothing is posted, and nothing is logged.
- **Any other status, or any other content type on a `200`**: nothing is posted. The response is logged, without the
  URL or the code.
- **Empty, or made only of markup**: nothing is posted.

A reply goes into the room the event is about, and only while the bot is still a member of it. A `joined` event can be
answered the same way as a mention, so a bot can say hello when it joins.

### Delivery rules

- Timeouts: 5 seconds to connect, 10 seconds to write and to read. A bot that needs longer should answer `204` and post
...
## Known limits and follow-ups

- The code isn't encrypted at rest. The app doesn't configure Active Record encryption keys, and the code has to be
  shown on the list. Adding encryption would mean adding keys to deployments, and `find_by(code:)` would need
  deterministic encryption.
- There's no way to rotate a code yet. Deleting and recreating the bot is the workaround. A "Regenerate code" action
  is the natural next step.
- No rate limiting on the bot endpoint. A leaked code can flood a room until its bot is deleted.
- SQL debug logs show the literal values SQLite queries use, including bot codes and session tokens, so don't run
  production at `RAILS_LOG_LEVEL=debug`.
- Bot-authored messages don't show a "bot" badge. The author name is the only marker.
- Neither bot text nor attachments have a size limit, the same as people's messages. A very large body is read
  into memory in full.
- There's no `left` event. A bot isn't told when it's removed from a room, so a bot that's removed doesn't know it's
  no longer in the room until it tries to post there. Like `joined`, it would fit alongside `mention`.
- System tests need a chromedriver. They didn't run in the sandbox this was built in (it has no network to download
  one). The UI was checked with controller tests, and by driving a running server in headless Chromium over the DevTools
  protocol: the form, the composer's autocomplete, posting a mention, and the native `confirm()` on delete. The
  open-rooms switch was checked the same way, along with a `joined` job running through the async queue adapter after a
  closed room was created with the bot in it.
"
}

cd /app && cat > /tmp/docs_edit.rb <<'RUBY'
p = "docs/bots.md"
s = File.read(p)

def replace_once(s, old, new)
  raise "not found: #{old[0, 70].inspect}" unless s.scan(old).size == 1
  s.sub(old) { new }
end

# Model: suspension is part of what a bot is.
s = replace_once(s, <<~OLD, <<~NEW)
  Permissions reuse `User#can_administer?(record)`
OLD
  - A bot can be suspended for flooding or for failing webhooks. It keeps everything it has, but can't post or get
    webhooks until an administrator reactivates it (see [Misbehaving bots](#misbehaving-bots)).

  Permissions reuse `User#can_administer?(record)`
NEW

# Web UI: the suspended state and the Reactivate button.
s = replace_once(s, <<~OLD, <<~NEW)
  - Forms that fail validation re-render with status 422.
OLD
  - A suspended bot shows "Suspended" and the reason, to everyone who can see it. Administrators also get a "Reactivate"
    button, which asks for confirmation with the native `confirm()` (see [Reactivation](#reactivation)).
  - Forms that fail validation re-render with status 422.
NEW

# Limits per member: suspended bots still count.
s = replace_once(s, <<~OLD, <<~NEW)
  - Administrators aren't limited: `User#can_add_bots?` is always true for them.
OLD
  - Suspended bots still count, since they still exist (see [Misbehaving bots](#misbehaving-bots)).
  - Administrators aren't limited: `User#can_add_bots?` is always true for them.
NEW

# HTTP API: the new statuses, and the order the checks run in.
s = replace_once(s, <<~OLD, <<~NEW)
  | Empty or whitespace-only body and no attachment               | `422 Unprocessable Content`  |

  Checks run in that order, so an unknown code gets 401 whatever the room is. A response never includes the code.
OLD
  | Suspended bot                                                 | `403 Forbidden`              |
  | Cooling down, or the message would go over the limit          | `429 Too Many Requests`, with `Retry-After` in seconds |
  | Empty or whitespace-only body and no attachment               | `422 Unprocessable Content`  |

  Checks run in that order, so an unknown code gets 401 whatever the room is, and a suspended bot gets 403 whatever the
  room or body is. During a cooldown every attempt gets 429, whatever the room or body is, and each one counts towards
  suspension (see [Misbehaving bots](#misbehaving-bots)). A response never includes the code.
NEW

# Webhooks: suspended bots aren't called.
s = replace_once(s, <<~OLD, <<~NEW)
  - The bot is active, has a webhook, and is a member of the room the message was posted to. A bot that has left the room
    isn't called.
OLD
  - The bot is active, isn't suspended, has a webhook, and is a member of the room the message was posted to. A bot that
    has left the room isn't called, and a suspended bot is never called.
NEW

# Answering: replies are subject to the limits.
s = replace_once(s, <<~OLD, <<~NEW)
  A reply goes into the room the event is about, and only while the bot is still a member of it. A `joined` event can be
  answered the same way as a mention, so a bot can say hello when it joins.
OLD
  A reply goes into the room the event is about, and only while the bot is still a member of it. A `joined` event can be
  answered the same way as a mention, so a bot can say hello when it joins.

  A reply is posted under the same limits as the bot API. It counts towards the message limit, and a reply that's refused
  (during a cooldown, or past the limit) is dropped without an error. See [Misbehaving bots](#misbehaving-bots).
NEW

# Delivery rules: what counts as a failure.
s = replace_once(s, <<~OLD, <<~NEW)
  - There are no retries. A failed call is logged and dropped.
OLD
  - There are no retries. A failed call is logged and dropped. A failed call also counts towards suspending the bot, since
    ten in a row suspend it (see [Misbehaving bots](#misbehaving-bots)).
NEW

# Known limits: rate limiting now exists.
s = replace_once(s, <<~OLD, <<~NEW)
  - No rate limiting on the bot endpoint. A leaked code can flood a room until its bot is deleted.
OLD
  - The limits are per bot, and fixed in code. A leaked code can post at the limit (ten messages in ten seconds) until its
    bot is suspended or deleted. Stopping a bot that's posting within the limit, but in a way that's still unwanted, is
    left to the administrator.
NEW

  closed room was created with the bot in it. The suspension flow was checked the same way: a flood over the HTTP API,
  the bots page's "Suspended" state, and the "Reactivate" confirm, dismissed and then accepted.
NEW

misbehaving = <<~'NEW'
  ## Misbehaving bots

  A bot that floods a room, or whose webhook keeps failing, is suspended automatically. A suspended bot can't post or get
  webhooks, and only an administrator can bring it back.

  ### Flooding

  - A bot may post at most **10 messages in any 10 seconds**. Messages posted through the bot API and webhook replies
    both count. Only messages that are actually posted count: a refused attempt isn't a message.
  - The window slides. A message counts for 10 seconds from when it was posted, so a bot that posts once a second is never
    refused.
  - The message that goes over the limit is refused with `429 Too Many Requests` and `Retry-After`, the seconds left, and
    starts a **30-second cooldown**. A webhook reply that goes over is dropped.
  - During the cooldown, every attempt to post gets 429, whatever the room or body. Webhook replies are dropped. The
    cooldown doesn't extend, so `Retry-After` counts down to it.
  - **Five attempts during one cooldown suspend the bot.** The fifth attempt still gets 429. From then on the API answers
    403. The count starts again with each new cooldown.

  ### Failing webhooks

  - A delivery **succeeds on any `2xx`**. Anything else is a failed delivery: another status (a redirect counts, since
    redirects aren't followed), a timeout, a connection error, or an address that's refused (a private address, or a host
    that doesn't resolve). A `200` whose reply is too large, or isn't a reply type, is still a success, since the bot
    answered.
  - A successful delivery resets the count. **Ten failed deliveries in a row suspend the bot.**
  - A webhook that's refused a reply still counts as delivered. Only the delivery itself is counted.

  ### Suspension

  A suspended bot:

  - gets `403 Forbidden` from the bot API, before its room or body is checked;
  - gets no webhooks, of either kind, and joins it makes while suspended aren't announced (see
    [Open rooms](#open-rooms));
  - keeps its rooms, memberships, messages and code, and still counts towards its owner's bot limit;
  - stays on `/bots`, marked "Suspended" with the reason: "Went over its limit of 10 messages in 10 seconds, then kept
    trying during the 30-second cooldown." or "Its webhook failed 10 times in a row."

  The reason is shown to everyone who can see the bot: its creator, and administrators.

  ### Reactivation

  Only administrators can reactivate a suspended bot, from `/bots`, with the "Reactivate" button. Its creator can't. The
  button uses `data-turbo-confirm`, so the browser's native `confirm()` asks first, and cancelling it changes nothing.
  The endpoint is `POST /bots/:bot_id/reactivation` (`Bots::ReactivationsController`).

  Reactivating clears the cooldown and both counts, so the bot starts from a clean state. It doesn't clear the message
  window, though. A flooding bot's messages from the last 10 seconds still count, so its next message after reactivation
  may be refused, starting a fresh cooldown. Waiting out the window avoids that. Reactivating a bot that isn't suspended
  does nothing.

  ### Implementation notes

  - State lives on `bots`: `suspended_at` and `suspension_reason` (`Bot::Suspension`), `cooldown_until` and
    `cooldown_attempts`, and `consecutive_webhook_failures`. The limits are constants in `Bot::Flooding` and
    `Bot::Suspension`, not settings.
  - Recent messages are counted from the `messages` table, through its `creator_id` index, so there's no second record of
    posting to keep in step.
  - The window check, the cooldown bookkeeping and the message insert run in one transaction under the bot's row lock
    (`Bot#post_message`). An API call and a webhook reply can't both see room under the limit. SQLite runs write
    transactions one at a time anyway. Attachments are processed after the commit, so image work doesn't hold the lock.
  - Refusals are raised after the transaction commits, since raising inside it would roll back the cooldown bookkeeping.
    The controller turns `Bot::Suspended` into 403 and `Bot::RateLimited` into 429, with `Retry-After`.
  - The cooldown check runs before the room and body are checked (`Bot#refuse_during_cooldown!`, called from
    `Bots::MessagesController`), so every attempt during a cooldown counts. The webhook path checks inside `post_message`.
  - `Retry-After` is rounded up to whole seconds, so a client that waits that long isn't refused again.
  - Suspended bots are left out of `Bot.with_active_webhook`, which the mention and joined paths both use.
  - A webhook call holds a copy of its bot. If the bot is deleted while the call is in flight, its counts can't be
    updated, so the delivery is dropped quietly (`Bot::Webhook#deliver`).
  - Log lines name the bot by id and say why, but never show its code or URL.
  - Tests that travel in time should use whole seconds. `travel_to` drops fractions unless `with_usec: true` is passed,
    which can make a cooldown look one second shorter than it is.

  ### Open follow-ups

  - Nothing tells the creator that their bot was suspended. Bots don't send notifications yet.
  - Administrators can't see how close a bot is to a limit. A count of recent messages or failures on the bots page would
    help diagnose a bot before it's suspended.

cd /app && cat > /tmp/docs_fix3.rb <<'RUBY'
p = "docs/bots.md"
s = File.read(p)
row_susp = "| Suspended bot                                                 | `403 Forbidden`              |\n"
row_429 = "| Cooling down, or the message would go over the limit          | `429 Too Many Requests`, with `Retry-After` in seconds |\n"
row_404 = "| Room doesn't exist, or the bot isn't a member of it           | `404 Not Found`              |\n"
raise "rows" unless [row_susp, row_429, row_404].all? { |r| s.include?(r) }
s = s.sub(row_susp + row_429 + row_404, row_susp + row_429 + row_404) # no-op guard
unknown = "| Unknown, deleted or banned bot code                           | `401 Unauthorized`           |\n"
raise "unknown" unless s.include?(unknown)
s = s.sub(row_susp + row_429 + row_404 + "", "")  if false
# Rebuild the block in check order: 401, 403, 429, 404, 422.
block_start = s.index(unknown)
block_end = s.index("| Empty or whitespace-only body and no attachment")
old_block = s[block_start...block_end]
new_block = unknown + row_susp + row_429 + row_404
s = s[0...block_start] + new_block + s[block_end..]
s = s.sub("bots never sign in.\n\n- A bot can be suspended", "bots never sign in.\n- A bot can be suspended")
File.write(p, s)
puts old_block
puts "---"
puts new_block

    assert_equal 30, error.retry_after
    assert_equal 10, @bot.user.messages.count
    assert_in_delta 30.seconds.from_now, @bot.reload.cooldown_until, 1
  end

  test "messages from other people in the room don't count towards the bot's limit" do
    10.times { @room.messages.create!(creator: users(:kevin), body: "Hello") }

    10.times { post_as_bot }

    assert_equal 10, @bot.user.messages.count
  end

  test "each bot has its own limit" do
    other = create_bot(name: "Release Bot", add_to_all_open_rooms: true)
    10.times { post_as_bot }

    assert_nothing_raised { other.post_message(@room, body: Bot.html_from_text("Hello")) }
  end

  test "the window slides: a bot that posts once a second is never refused" do
    travel_to Time.current do
      31.times do
        post_as_bot
        travel 1.second
      end
    end

    assert_equal 31, @bot.user.messages.count
    assert_nil @bot.reload.cooldown_until
  end

  test "the window is the last ten seconds, so older messages stop counting as the window moves on" do
    start = Time.current.change(usec: 0)

    travel_to start do
      5.times { post_as_bot }
    end

    travel_to start + 5 do
      5.times { post_as_bot } # Ten in the last ten seconds
    end

    travel_to start + 10 do
      5.times { post_as_bot } # Only the five from start + 5 are still in the window
      assert_raises(Bot::RateLimited) { post_as_bot }
    end

    assert_equal 15, @bot.user.messages.count
  end

  test "attempts during the cooldown are refused, with the seconds left as retry_after" do
    travel_to Time.current do
      10.times { post_as_bot }
      assert_raises(Bot::RateLimited) { post_as_bot }

      travel 10.seconds
      error = assert_raises(Bot::RateLimited) { post_as_bot }

      assert_equal 20, error.retry_after
    end
  end

  test "retry_after rounds up, so waiting it out is always enough" do
    travel_to Time.current do
      10.times { post_as_bot }
      assert_raises(Bot::RateLimited) { post_as_bot }

      travel 10.5.seconds, with_usec: true
      error = assert_raises(Bot::RateLimited) { post_as_bot }

      assert_equal 20, error.retry_after
    end
  end

  test "the cooldown is 30 seconds, after which the bot can post again" do
    start = Time.current.change(usec: 0)

    travel_to start do
      10.times { post_as_bot }
      assert_raises(Bot::RateLimited) { post_as_bot }
    end

    travel_to start + 29.9, with_usec: true do
      assert_raises(Bot::RateLimited) { post_as_bot }
    end

    travel_to start + 30 do
      assert_nothing_raised { post_as_bot }
    end
  end

    assert_equal 10, @bot.user.messages.count

    assert_equal 1, @bot.reload.cooldown_attempts

  test "an attempt checked against the cooldown outside it is let through" do

    assert_equal 0, @bot.reload.cooldown_attempts

# limits as the bot API (see Bot::Flooding), so a reply can be refused, and then it isn't posted.
class Bot::Webhook
  OPEN_TIMEOUT = 5 # seconds
  READ_TIMEOUT = 10 # seconds
  MAX_REPLY_SIZE = 1.megabyte
  REPLY_CONTENT_TYPES = %w[ text/plain text/html ]

  class ReplyTooLarge < StandardError; end

    Net::ProtocolError, Net::HTTPBadResponse, Zlib::Error,
    RestrictedHTTP::Violation, Surfguard::Unresolvable
  ]

  attr_reader :bot, :payload

  delegate :room, to: :payload

  def initialize(bot, payload)
    @bot, @payload = bot, payload
  end

    # Suspended bots, and those whose user is banned or deactivated, aren't called. Jobs check this too, but a bot can be
    # suspended while its job waits in the queue.
    return unless bot.webhook_active?

    delivered, reply = attempt

    if delivered
      bot.webhook_delivered
      post_reply(reply) if reply.present? && bot_in_room?
    else
      bot.webhook_failed
    end
  rescue ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound
    # The bot was deleted while its webhook was being called, so there's nothing left to count or post.
  end

  private
    def url
      @url ||= URI.parse(bot.webhook_url)
    end

    # Returns whether the bot answered with a 2xx, and its reply. A call that gets no response at all is logged, and counts
    # as not delivered.
    def attempt
      fetch_reply
    rescue *DELIVERY_FAILURES => e
      Rails.logger.warn "Webhook for bot #{bot.id} produced no reply: #{e.class} #{e.message}"
      [ false, nil ]
    end

    # changes in between. Redirects aren't followed, so a bot can't send us somewhere that wasn't checked.
    def fetch_reply
      ip = RestrictedHTTP::PrivateNetworkGuard.resolve(url.host)
